name: pear crumble
instructions:
Nicole Rucker's Ginger-y Pear Crumble Pie from Fat + Flour (page 134) — a 9-inch pie: pastry crust on the bottom, ginger-honey pear filling, buttery crumble on top. Transcribed from the book. MY BUILD DIFFERS: I skip the candied ginger, and I use the [[rolled-oats-pie-top]] instead of her streusel-like crumble — plus a drippings glaze on the crust (see notes).

MAKES ONE 9-INCH PIE.

=== FOR THE GINGER CRUMBLE ===

- 1 cup (125g) unbleached all-purpose flour
- 1/4 cup packed (53g) light-brown sugar
- 1/4 cup (50g) granulated sugar
- pinch of Diamond Crystal kosher salt
- 2 tbsp (30g) finely chopped candied ginger (I SKIP THIS — see notes)
- 1/2 cup (113g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled

=== TO ASSEMBLE THE PIE ===

- unbleached all-purpose flour for rolling the dough
- 1/2 recipe Fat + Flour Pie Dough (page 114 of the book), made in advance and chilled

=== FOR THE FILLING ===

- 2 1/2 lb (1.36kg) FIRM BUT FRAGRANT pears, such as Bartlett, Green Anjou, or Comice (see notes on pear choice)
- 1/2 cup (100g) granulated sugar
- 1 tsp (3g) Diamond Crystal kosher salt
- 3 tbsp (30g) cornstarch
- 3 tbsp (63g) wildflower honey
- 2 tbsp (28g) lemon juice
- 1 tbsp (14g) bourbon (optional)
- 1 tbsp (7g) freshly grated ginger

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. MAKE THE CRUMBLE TOPPING: whisk the flour, sugars, salt, and candied ginger (if using) together in a small bowl; add the melted butter and mix until it resembles a buttery crumble.
2. PREHEAT the oven to 375°F (190°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
3. ASSEMBLE THE PIE: lightly flour a work surface. Remove the dough from the fridge and remove the plastic. If chilled overnight it needs to temper before rolling — usually 10-15 minutes. Once pliable, roll the disc out to a 12-inch circle, flouring as needed to prevent sticking. Transfer to a 9-inch pie plate and trim the edge to allow 1 inch of overhang. Roll or fold the hanging edge over itself, then crimp with thumb and forefinger. PUT THE CRIMPED CRUST IN THE FREEZER while you prepare the filling.
4. MAKE THE FILLING: peel and core the pears, and slice them 1/4 inch thick. Whisk the sugar, salt, and cornstarch together in a large bowl; add the pears and toss. Whisk the honey, lemon juice, bourbon (if using), and grated ginger together in a small bowl, add to the pears, and gently toss so all the fruit is coated.
5. IMMEDIATELY pour the filling and any collected juices into the crust, and scatter the crumble over the top. (Don't let the fruit sit in the sugar — see the maceration warning in notes.)
6. CHILL the whole pie in the freezer for 10 minutes, then place it on the prepared baking sheet and bake on the center rack until the crust is a deep golden brown and the juices from the pie are boiling — about 1 FULL HOUR, possibly longer.
7. COOL the pie for 1 hour before eating, to allow the juices to settle and continue thickening.
8. LEFTOVERS: store in the fridge. Warm slices of the cold pie at 375°F for 15 minutes before eating for best results.
notes:
=== SOURCE ===

Nicole Rucker, Fat + Flour: The Art of a Simple Bake, page 134 ('Ginger-y Pear Crumble Pie'). Her headnote: there's a video somewhere of her teaching a celeb to make pear pie on late-night TV — search Nicole Rucker + Seth Meyers + pears. The crust is 1/2 recipe of her Fat + Flour Pie Dough (page 114 of the book — not transcribed here).

=== I SKIP THE CANDIED GINGER ===

The crumble calls for 2 tbsp finely chopped candied ginger; I don't use that part. The fresh grated ginger in the filling stays.

=== MY TOPPING — ROLLED OATS PIE TOP, NOT HER STREUSEL CRUMBS ===

I didn't use her streusel-like crumbs — I used the [[rolled-oats-pie-top]] (3/4 cup flour, 3/4 cup rolled oats, 1 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup cold unsalted butter, 1/4 tsp salt, all in a food processor).

WHY A TOPPING IS STRUCTURAL HERE: pears are HARDER than apples when not ripe, and I think a topping like this (or a pie lid) is NECESSARY to get the pie to come together — unlike [[apple-pie]], which seems to be OK with a covered → uncovered stage.

=== DRIPPINGS GLAZE ON THE CRUST ===

Bake at 375°F. Before baking, I used a brush to glaze the outside of the pie crust with the liquid drippings of the filling — there's more overall liquid to work with due to the topping's lower flour/butter content.

=== GINGER CALIBRATION — MEDICINAL HOT, MELLOWS COOL, STILL A BIT STRONG ===

The fresh ginger root makes the pie taste MEDICINAL when it first comes out of the oven. As it cools, that sharpness disappears and it tastes better (the 1-hour cooling rule is doing flavor work here, not just thickening). But even cooled I still think it's a bit strong/floral.

WANT TO TRY:
- ~1 tsp GROUND GINGER instead of the fresh root.
- A mix of GINGER AND CARDAMOM, which I find is a common pairing.
- HER BOURBON (untested by me) — might be the trick to balancing the ginger.

=== PEAR CHOICE — FIRM BUT FRAGRANT, RIPE-ISH NOT RIPE ===

Rucker's key to success: choose pears that are RIPE-ISH BUT FRAGRANT, not fully ripe. Too-ripe pears turn to mush in the bake and you end up with (delicious) soggy baby food in a crumble and crust. Firm-but-fragrant ensures the fruit holds its structure. Bartlett, Green Anjou, or Comice.

=== DON'T LET THE FRUIT MACERATE — THE SOUPY-PIE WARNING ===

Very important: do NOT allow the fruit to sit in the sugar for any length of time — the sugar pulls the juices out and you get a soupy pie ('a li'l soupy situation'). This is why the crust goes in the freezer BEFORE the filling is made, and the filling is poured and topped IMMEDIATELY after tossing. Mix, pour, crumble, bake — no pauses.

=== TIMING NOTES ===

- FREEZER, TWICE: the crimped empty crust chills in the freezer while the filling comes together, and the assembled pie gets 10 more freezer minutes before baking.
- DONENESS: deep golden crust + VISIBLY BOILING juices. A full hour, possibly longer — don't pull early.
- THE HOUR OF COOLING is structural — the juices settle and continue thickening off-heat. Same wisdom as [[apple-pie]].
- The reheat-from-cold move (375°F for 15 min) is her explicit recommendation for leftovers.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[rolled-oats-pie-top]]: my topping for this pie — the component recipe.
- [[apple-pie]]: the other fruit pie (softer fruit — gets away without a structural topping).
- [[sweet-potato-pies-and-galettes]]: in its pot-pie era ('turnip yam pie'), the other pie where fresh ginger did the lifting — and where too much ginger was the documented failure mode (same hazard here). Its active build has since gone dill-forward.
original_chef: Nicole Rucker — Fat + Flour: The Art of a Simple Bake, page 134.
